description:
fz-sc8.227 (#633) held BoundValue::Transport's lanes inline (SmallVec<[W; 4]>). That made every bound value larger, and programs that read no binary slower: at the CI profile (opt-level 1) fixture 01254 on interp went from 52.2G instructions / about 11.1G cycles to 47.7G / about 11.7G, and 01294 from 54.6G / 11.8G to 49.0G / 12.2G. Develop's coverage step is red from 107558626 onward: 01254 and 01294 exceed 20 s CPU on interp.

With the lanes back in a Vec and the other three changes of fz-sc8.227 kept (ExternTy::wire, extern_argument_words over slices, no pending-rest room until a rest is matched), same profile: 01254 46.9G / about 10.2G cycles, 01294 47.9G / about 10.7G, byte walk 24.8G / 4.9G (5.0G / 23.3G with inline lanes, 5.8G / 30.1G before fz-sc8.227). So the inline lanes bought nothing on the walk and cost 10 to 13% elsewhere.

Done when: BoundValue::Transport.lanes is a Vec again, the three other changes stand, and the coverage step passes 01254 and 01294 on develop's push run.
title: A lane-form value in the interpreter is held in a list, not inline
